matches.rationale: Ground truth concerns ElasticMM's overstated TTFT and throughput metrics in the abstract vs. experimental figures. All findings relate to a completely different paper about tactile neural networks and rodent somatosensory cortex, not multimodal LLM serving.

Ground truth describes a contradiction in the definition of burst tolerance between text and Equation 1 in ElasticMM's load balancing method. The findings discuss a different paper on tactile processing with no mention of burst tolerance or load balancing.

Ground truth identifies missing baseline configuration details (batch sizes, KV cache) for vLLM and DistServe in ElasticMM experiments. The findings are from a neuroscience paper with no relation to LLM serving systems or these baselines.

Ground truth concerns inflated throughput claims for ShareGPT-4o dataset in ElasticMM (4.5× vs actual 3.1×). The findings discuss tactile neural networks and whisker simulations, not multimodal LLM throughput metrics.

Ground truth identifies unsupported generalization about ElasticMM's applicability across all MLLM architectures based on testing only two models. The findings are from a different paper on rodent somatosensory models with no MLLM architecture claims.

Ground truth describes fabrication of reference [61] (Zhang et al. 2024) in ElasticMM's related work on multimodal inference stage separation. The findings discuss fabricated references in a tactile neuroscience paper (Grant 2025), a completely different context.

Ground truth identifies inconsistent cost terms between Equations 2 and 3 in ElasticMM's optimization framework (switching from decode to prefill context). The findings discuss whisker array arrangements and RNN update equations in a neuroscience paper.

Ground truth concerns missing ethical disclosures about web-scraped datasets (VisualWebInstruct, ShareGPT-4o) in ElasticMM experiments. The findings discuss mouse neural data and whisker simulations with different ethical concerns.

Ground truth identifies promotional language claiming ElasticMM 'completely eliminates all inference bottlenecks' in the introduction. The findings discuss overstated claims about neural alignment in a tactile processing paper, not LLM inference.

Ground truth describes mischaracterization of prefix caching as part of scheduling in ElasticMM's abstract when it's actually a separate optimization. The findings discuss context misalignment in force simulation parameters, a completely different technical domain.

Ground truth concerns cherry-picked presentation of ablation study results in ElasticMM, claiming equal contributions when Figure 8 shows otherwise. The findings discuss neural alignment saturation claims in a neuroscience paper.

Ground truth identifies unfair comparison where ElasticMM uses optimized CUDA kernels unavailable to baselines. The findings discuss missing hyperparameter details for whisking datasets, a different experimental protocol issue in a different paper.

Ground truth concerns ElasticMM's conclusion claiming universal SLO compliance when experiments show conditional performance. The findings discuss overstated neural alignment claims in a tactile processing paper, not SLO guarantees.

Ground truth identifies false attribution of encoder-decoder MLLM architectures to Vaswani et al.'s Transformer paper. The findings discuss fabricated references in a neuroscience paper about tactile processing, completely different subject matter.

Ground truth concerns missing discussion of ElasticMM's limitations and societal impacts in the conclusion. The findings discuss omitted ethical reflections on neural dataset scarcity in a neuroscience paper, different context and domain.
